alt: A panel titled Why Do We Need LSTM. A basic RNN meets long sequences, then vanishing or exploding gradient, then difficulty with long-term dependencies, so we need better memory control. What if the network could decide what to keep and what to forget.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled LSTM, Long Short-Term Memory. LSTM is an improved type of RNN designed to handle long-term dependencies more effectively. Basic RNN has a memory problem, LSTM gives better control of information. Key idea: LSTM uses gates to control the flow of information.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Why Does LSTM Need Gates. Not all information is important, as in I live in Mumbai, I love pizza, I am studying Computer Engineering. LSTM decides what to keep, what to forget, what new information to add and what to output. Gates control the flow of information.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled LSTM Cell, Big Picture. The cell has a forget gate, input gate, cell state and output gate. At every time step it receives the previous hidden state, current input and previous cell state and produces a new cell state and new hidden state.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Cell State vs Hidden State. Cell state is long-term memory that carries important information through the sequence. Hidden state is current or short-term information used to produce the current output and passed to the next step.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Forget Gate, What Should We Forget. The previous memory says I live in Mumbai and the new sentence says I moved to Pune. The forget gate uses a sigmoid giving values between 0 and 1, where 0 means forget and 1 means keep.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Input Gate, What New Information Should We Store. The input gate looks at the current input, selects the important information and adds it to memory, using values between 0 and 1 to control how much is stored.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Updating the Cell State. LSTM makes two decisions, forget information that is no longer useful and add important new information. Old memory I live in Mumbai becomes I live in Pune.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Output Gate, What Should We Output. The updated cell state goes through the output gate, which selects the relevant information to become the hidden state or output. The cell may remember many things but the output may only need Pune.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled How Does an LSTM Work. From the previous cell state, the forget gate removes old information, the input gate adds new information, giving the updated cell state, and the output gate selects what to output as the hidden state. The four questions are what to forget, add, remember and output.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled LSTM Numerical Example. Forget gate 0.2 times old memory 10 gives 2 retained. Input gate 0.8 times new information 5 gives 4 added. New cell state is 2 plus 4, which is 6.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A table of RNN versus LSTM. RNN has a hidden state, a basic memory mechanism, can struggle with long-term dependencies, has no gates, is simpler and suffers vanishing gradients. LSTM has hidden state plus cell state, a special memory mechanism, is designed for long-term dependencies, uses gates, is more complex and gates preserve useful information.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled How Does Information Flow Through LSTM. The current input x t, the previous hidden state h t minus 1 and the previous cell state c t minus 1 go into the LSTM cell, which gives the new cell state c t and the new hidden state h t, then the output.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled How Is the Cell State Updated. The forget gate removes unnecessary information from the previous cell state, the input gate adds useful new information from the current input, and the new cell state is old useful information plus new useful information.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled How Does LSTM Produce an Output. New cell state, then output gate, then select relevant information, then new hidden state, then output.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled How Does LSTM Learn. Forward pass over t1 to t4 gives a prediction and a loss. The error is propagated backward using backpropagation through time. LSTM uses the same BPTT, and the cell state gives a better pathway for information and gradients across time.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Complete LSTM Working. Current input, forget gate (remove old info), input gate (add new info), updated cell state, output gate (select relevant info), hidden state, output. Training goes forward, prediction, loss, BPTT, weight update.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled LSTM for Language Understanding. In the sentence I grew up in India, after many years I moved to another country, I still speak blank, the important information India appeared much earlier, and LSTM uses it to predict Hindi.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Why Use LSTM Instead of Basic RNN. For a short sequence t1 to t4 an RNN can work well. For a long sequence up to t50 with important information from earlier steps LSTM is more suitable.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled GRU, Gated Recurrent Unit. RNN has the long-term dependency problem, LSTM is one solution and GRU is another. GRU is another type of RNN that uses gates to control information. It uses two main gates, the update gate and the reset gate.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled GRU Cell, Big Picture. The previous hidden state and current input go into the GRU cell, which gives the new hidden state and then the output. Unlike LSTM, GRU does not have a separate cell state and mainly uses the hidden state to carry information.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Reset Gate, How Much Past Information Should We Use. The reset gate decides how much of the previous information should be considered when processing the new input. 0 means ignore most previous information, 1 means use most of it.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Update Gate, What Should We Keep. The update gate decides how much information should come from the previous hidden state and from the new candidate information, controlling how much old information is kept and how much new information is used.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Hidden State, GRU memory. In GRU there is no separate cell state. The hidden state carries the information forward from h t minus 1 to h t to h t plus 1.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled How Is the GRU Hidden State Updated, in six steps: look at the previous hidden state and the current input, use the reset gate, create the candidate information, use the update gate, and produce the new hidden state.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A strip titled Complete GRU Working: current input, reset gate, candidate information, update gate, new hidden state, output. Four questions: reset gate asks how much past information to use, candidate asks what new information to create, update gate asks how much old or new to keep, hidden state asks what to carry forward.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled GRU Forward Pass for I love AI. The GRU processes the sequence one time step at a time, taking the current input and previous hidden state and giving a new hidden state h1, h2 and h3.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Simple GRU Numerical Example. Previous hidden state 10, new candidate information 4, update gate 0.7. New hidden state is 0.7 times 10 plus 0.3 times 4, which is 7 plus 1.2, which is 8.2.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A table of LSTM versus GRU. LSTM has cell state and hidden state, 3 gates (forget, input, output), more complex, more parameters. GRU has only the hidden state, 2 gates (reset, update), simpler, fewer parameters.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The LSTM cell. The cell state line carries c t minus 1 through a multiply by the forget gate and an add of the input gate times the candidate. The output gate times tanh of the cell state gives the hidden state. The gate equations are f t, i t, candidate c hat t and o t, each a sigmoid or tanh of a weight times h t minus 1 and x t plus a bias.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The internal structure of a basic RNN unit and an LSTM unit. The RNN unit has one layer combining x t and h t minus 1. The LSTM unit has an input gate, an input modulation gate, a forget gate and an output gate with the cell state c t minus 1 passing through to c t.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: An LSTM block with three parts. Part 1 forgets irrelevant information from the long-term memory C t minus 1, part 2 adds or updates new information, part 3 passes the updated information on. H t minus 1 is the short-term memory.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: A chain of LSTM cells A, with the input x t entering the middle cell, four small gate boxes inside it, and the hidden state h t going out of each cell.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The GRU cell. The previous hidden state h t minus 1 and input x t go through the reset gate r t and the update gate z t. The reset gate output scales h t minus 1 to make the candidate hidden state h tilde t, and the update gate mixes h t minus 1 with the candidate to give the new hidden state h t.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The GRU equations: reset gate r t, update gate z t, candidate state h tilde t equal to tanh of W h applied to x t and r t times h t minus 1, and the new hidden state as a mix of h t minus 1 and the candidate with weights 1 minus z t and z t. The three gates are explained below.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Computing the reset gate R t and the update gate Z t in a GRU. The hidden state H t minus 1 and the input X t are concatenated and sent to two fully connected layers with a sigmoid activation, one for each gate.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Computing the hidden state in a GRU. The reset gate scales the previous hidden state, a tanh layer makes the candidate hidden state, and the update gate Z t blends the old hidden state with the candidate through 1 minus Z t to give H t.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut
